title: Rugby Union: overview
d: Rugby Union is a team ball sport played 15 players per side.
definition: Rugby Union is a team ball sport played 15 players per side.
description: Rugby Union is a team ball sport. score more points than the opponent. The contest is played 15 players per side, and the side that 5 per try, 2 per conversion, 3 per penalty or drop goal; most points wins wins. Codified at Rugby School (1845) and the RFU (1871); the Rugby World Cup began in 1987. The sport is governed by official laws that cover the field of play, equipment, players, officials, scoring, fouls, and conduct; this database walks through every one of those areas so a newcomer can follow a full match with understanding.

title: The objective
d: The objective of Rugby Union is: score more points than the opponent.
definition: The objective of Rugby Union is: score more points than the opponent.
description: Every rule in Rugby Union exists to serve one objective: score more points than the opponent. All tactics, positions, and scoring flow from that single aim. Beginners should fix the objective in mind first, because every foul, stoppage, and strategy in the sport is judged against whether it fairly advances or unfairly blocks that objective. Coaches return to it constantly: if a play does not serve the objective, it is the wrong play.

facts.objective: score more points than the opponent

title: Scoring system
d: In Rugby Union, scoring works as follows: 5 per try, 2 per conversion, 3 per penalty or drop goal; most points wins.
definition: In Rugby Union, scoring works as follows: 5 per try, 2 per conversion, 3 per penalty or drop goal; most points wins.
description: Scoring in Rugby Union: 5 per try, 2 per conversion, 3 per penalty or drop goal; most points wins. Knowing exactly what counts, and how much, changes how you watch: every attack is shaped by the scoring system, and comebacks are measured against it. Scorekeepers record each score the moment it happens, and at most levels the scoreboard is the official record unless a protest is filed under the competition rules.

facts.scoring: 5 per try, 2 per conversion, 3 per penalty or drop goal; most points wins

title: How games are won
d: Rugby Union: 5 per try, 2 per conversion, 3 per penalty or drop goal; most points wins.
definition: Rugby Union: 5 per try, 2 per conversion, 3 per penalty or drop goal; most points wins.
description: Winning Rugby Union comes down to the scoreboard: 5 per try, 2 per conversion, 3 per penalty or drop goal; most points wins. Because of that, late-game strategy everywhere in the sport is clock-and-score management — protecting a lead or chasing one changes every decision, from how much risk to take to when to slow play down or speed it up. Champions are often simply the teams that manage the winning condition best in the final minutes.

title: Ties and tiebreakers
d: Tied games in Rugby Union are resolved under the competition rules for the level of play.
definition: Tied games in Rugby Union are resolved under the competition rules for the level of play.
description: Not every contest in Rugby Union can end tied: league games may allow draws while knockout games must produce a winner through extra time, tiebreak procedures, or shootouts defined by the competition. Tiebreak rules are announced before play and never invented mid-game; players and coaches must know them, because they reshape tactics — a team may play for penalties, or gamble everything to avoid them.

facts.note: tiebreak rules are set by the competition, not improvised

title: Match duration
d: Rugby Union contests last: two 40-minute halves.
definition: Rugby Union contests last: two 40-minute halves.
description: A Rugby Union contest runs two 40-minute halves. Duration shapes fitness demands: athletes train to be sharp in the final stretch, not just the first. Timekeeping is an official duty — the clock, not the players, decides when it ends, and added or extra time exists to compensate for stoppages so the advertised duration is genuinely played.

title: Periods and breaks
d: Play in Rugby Union is divided into periods with breaks as defined for the competition.
definition: Play in Rugby Union is divided into periods with breaks as defined for the competition.
description: The two 40-minute halves in Rugby Union give coaches their main lever: adjustments, substitutions, and rest happen in the breaks. Teams plan for three phases — start fast, manage the middle, finish strong — and the side that uses its breaks better often wins the second half. Break length and number are fixed by the rules; exceeding them can draw penalties.

title: The venue
d: Rugby Union is played at: field max 100m by 70m with in-goal areas; H-shaped posts.
definition: Rugby Union is played at: field max 100m by 70m with in-goal areas; H-shaped posts.
description: The Rugby Union is part of the sport: field max 100m by 70m with in-goal areas; H-shaped posts. Dimensions, surfaces, and markings are standardized so records and tactics transfer between venues. Groundskeepers and officials inspect the venue before play; an unfit surface can postpone a contest. Players learn to read their venue — wind, sun, surface speed — because the same game plays differently in different buildings.

facts.venue: field max 100m by 70m with in-goal areas; H-shaped posts

title: Field dimensions
d: Regulation dimensions for Rugby Union: field max 100m by 70m with in-goal areas; H-shaped posts.
definition: Regulation dimensions for Rugby Union: field max 100m by 70m with in-goal areas; H-shaped posts.
description: Regulation Rugby Union dimensions: field max 100m by 70m with in-goal areas; H-shaped posts. Lines are part of the field of play and officiated precisely — in or out, over the line or not, decides scores. Youth and amateur versions scale the dimensions down, but the proportions and the meaning of every line stay the same so skills transfer up to the full-size game.

facts.venue: field max 100m by 70m with in-goal areas; H-shaped posts

title: Playing surface
d: Rugby Union surfaces must be safe, level, and marked to regulation.
definition: Rugby Union surfaces must be safe, level, and marked to regulation.
description: The playing surface in Rugby Union must be safe, level, and marked to regulation. Surface changes tactics: fast surfaces reward speed and quick passing, slow or soft ones reward power and patience. Footwear and equipment rules usually assume a specific surface, and playing on the wrong one risks both injury and disqualification of the contest.

title: Essential equipment
d: Rugby Union requires: oval ball, boots, mouthguard; scrum cap optional.
definition: Rugby Union requires: oval ball, boots, mouthguard; scrum cap optional.
description: No one plays Rugby Union without: oval ball, boots, mouthguard; scrum cap optional. Equipment is inspected — illegal or unsafe gear is removed before play, and at higher levels every item must meet the governing body's specifications. Beginners should buy for safety and fit first, performance second; the right size matters more than the brand.

facts.equipment: oval ball, boots, mouthguard; scrum cap optional

title: The ball
d: The Rugby Union ball is specified by the laws: size, weight, and pressure are regulated.
definition: The Rugby Union ball is specified by the laws: size, weight, and pressure are regulated.
description: Where Rugby Union uses a ball, its size, weight, bounce, and pressure are fixed by the laws: oval ball, boots, mouthguard; scrum cap optional. Ball specs change the whole game — a lighter, livelier ball rewards touch, a heavier one rewards power. Match balls are approved and often supplied by the competition; warming up with the wrong spec builds the wrong feel.

facts.equipment: oval ball, boots, mouthguard; scrum cap optional

title: Protective gear
d: Protection in Rugby Union: required and recommended gear keeps players safe within the laws.
definition: Protection in Rugby Union: required and recommended gear keeps players safe within the laws.
description: Protection is part of the laws of Rugby Union, not an afterthought. Required and recommended gear exists because the sport's known injury patterns are known: the rules mandate the gear that prevents the common ones. Gear must fit and be worn correctly — loose or missing protection can keep a player off the field, and no contest is worth a preventable injury.

title: Team size
d: Rugby Union is played 15 players per side.
definition: Rugby Union is played 15 players per side.
description: Rugby Union is played 15 players per side. Numbers decide the geometry of the game: more players means more structure and specialization, fewer means more space and versatility. Every player must know the legal team size, because playing short — or with too many — brings penalties, and planned rotations are built around the allowed numbers.

title: Positions and roles
d: Positions in Rugby Union divide the work: each role has a zone, duties, and skills.
definition: Positions in Rugby Union divide the work: each role has a zone, duties, and skills.
description: Positions in Rugby Union exist to divide the 15 players per side into manageable jobs. Each role has a home zone, primary duties, and a skill profile; great teams are built by fitting people to roles, not roles to people. Beginners should learn one position deeply before roaming — mastery of a role teaches the whole game faster than playing everywhere badly.

title: Substitutions
d: Substitution rules in Rugby Union control how and when players may be replaced.
definition: Substitution rules in Rugby Union control how and when players may be replaced.
description: Substitutions in Rugby Union are a tactical weapon governed by strict procedure: only at stoppages, only through the official, only within the allowed number. Coaches plan substitution windows the way generals plan reserves — fresh legs at the right moment win tight games. Illegal substitution procedure can cost a team a player or a penalty.

title: Officials
d: Rugby Union is officiated by: referee plus two assistants and TMO.
definition: Rugby Union is officiated by: referee plus two assistants and TMO.
description: Rugby Union is officiated by referee plus two assistants and TMO. Officials are neutral arbiters of the laws: their decisions on matters of fact are final during play, and dissent is penalized. Knowing what each official watches helps players stay legal — most fouls are committed in full view of exactly the official assigned to that zone.

facts.officials: referee plus two assistants and TMO

title: The referee's role
d: The referee in Rugby Union enforces the laws, keeps time, and manages conduct.
definition: The referee in Rugby Union enforces the laws, keeps time, and manages conduct.
description: The referee's job in Rugby Union is bigger than blowing a whistle: enforcing the laws, keeping time, managing conduct, and protecting player safety — in that order. Players may ask for clarification respectfully; they may not dispute decisions. At every level, the referee's authority begins when they enter the venue and ends when they leave it.

facts.officials: referee plus two assistants and TMO

title: Key rule 1
d: The ball may only be passed backward or sideways; forward passes are penalized.
definition: The ball may only be passed backward or sideways; forward passes are penalized.
description: Key rule of Rugby Union (1 of 4): The ball may only be passed backward or sideways; forward passes are penalized.. This is one of the laws players break most often when learning the game, so officials watch it closely. Understanding the reason behind the rule — the unfair advantage it prevents — makes it easy to remember and to apply at speed. When in doubt during play, the safe choice is the one this rule describes.

facts.rule: The ball may only be passed backward or sideways; forward passes are penalized.

title: Fouls
d: Illegal play in Rugby Union draws fouls under the laws; persistent fouling draws cards or ejections.
definition: Illegal play in Rugby Union draws fouls under the laws; persistent fouling draws cards or ejections.
description: A foul in Rugby Union is illegal play as defined by the laws — not just rough play, but any act the rules forbid. Officials grade fouls by intent, danger, and advantage gained; persistent or cynical fouling draws escalating punishment. Smart players learn the exact line: physical right up to it, never across it.

title: Penalties
d: Fouls in Rugby Union are punished by free plays, spot penalties, or loss of possession per the laws.
definition: Fouls in Rugby Union are punished by free plays, spot penalties, or loss of possession per the laws.
description: Punishment in Rugby Union fits the foul: minor infringements restart play for the other side, serious ones award direct scoring chances or remove the offender. Penalty rules are deliberately severe enough that fouling is never a good trade — the team that stays disciplined keeps eleven (or its equivalent) on the field and wins the close ones.

title: Discipline and conduct
d: Misconduct in Rugby Union — dissent, dangerous play, unsporting behavior — is penalized, up to ejection.
definition: Misconduct in Rugby Union — dissent, dangerous play, unsporting behavior — is penalized, up to ejection.
description: The laws of Rugby Union punish misconduct on a ladder: warnings, cards, sin-bins, ejections, suspensions. Dissent, dangerous play, and unsporting behavior are treated as seriously as technical fouls, because the game depends on respect for officials and opponents. Captains are responsible for their team's conduct and speak to the referee for the side.

title: Basic strategy
d: Rugby Union strategy starts from the objective: score more points than the opponent.
definition: Rugby Union strategy starts from the objective: score more points than the opponent.
description: All Rugby Union strategy serves the objective: score more points than the opponent. The basic game plan is simple — win your individual battles, keep your shape, and take the chances the scoring system rewards most. Beginners win by doing simple things reliably; advanced players win by forcing opponents into mistakes while making none themselves.

facts.objective: score more points than the opponent

title: Offense
d: Attacking in Rugby Union means creating the scoring chances the rules reward.
definition: Attacking in Rugby Union means creating the scoring chances the rules reward.
description: Attacking Rugby Union is about manufacturing the highest-percentage chances the scoring system allows. Good offense is patient until the opening appears, then ruthless: create space, move the defense, and finish. The best attacks look simple because every player knows the plan two passes ahead.

title: Defense
d: Defending in Rugby Union means denying the objective: score more points than the opponent.
definition: Defending in Rugby Union means denying the objective: score more points than the opponent.
description: Defending Rugby Union starts from denying the objective: score more points than the opponent. Good defense is organized first and aggressive second — shape, communication, and patience, with pressure applied where the opponent is weakest. The great defensive teams all share one trait: every player defends, all the time, without being asked.

facts.objective: score more points than the opponent

title: Origins
d: Origins of Rugby Union: Codified at Rugby School (1845) and the RFU (1871); the Rugby World Cup began in 1987..
definition: Origins of Rugby Union: Codified at Rugby School (1845) and the RFU (1871); the Rugby World Cup began in 1987..
description: The origins of Rugby Union: Codified at Rugby School (1845) and the RFU (1871); the Rugby World Cup began in 1987.. Like most sports, it began as folk play and was formalized when clubs and schools wrote common rules so strangers could compete fairly. Those first written laws are the ancestor of every rule in this database — the game you watch today is their descendant.

facts.history: Codified at Rugby School (1845) and the RFU (1871); the Rugby World Cup began in 1987.

title: Modern era
d: Modern Rugby Union: professional leagues, world championships, and Olympic or global stages.
definition: Modern Rugby Union: professional leagues, world championships, and Olympic or global stages.
description: Modern Rugby Union grew through professional leagues, world championships, and global competition. Television and professionalism standardized the laws worldwide and turned the best players into full-time athletes. The modern game is faster, stronger, and more tactical than any earlier era — but it is played under the same essential objective the founders wrote down.

title: Variations
d: Rugby Union has official and informal variations with adjusted rules for numbers, space, and level.
definition: Rugby Union has official and informal variations with adjusted rules for numbers, space, and level.
description: Every major sport spawns variations: small-sided, beach, indoor, youth, and disability versions of Rugby Union all adjust numbers, space, and rules while keeping the soul of the game. Variations are where most people actually play — the full eleven-a-side (or equivalent) version is the tip of a much bigger pyramid.

title: Safety
d: Play Rugby Union safely: warm up, wear the required gear, follow the foul laws, and stop for injury.
definition: Play Rugby Union safely: warm up, wear the required gear, follow the foul laws, and stop for injury.
description: Safety in Rugby Union is part of the rules, not separate from them: warm up properly, wear every required piece of gear, respect the foul laws that exist to prevent injury, and stop play for any head injury or suspected serious harm. No game, drill, or tryout is worth playing hurt — the laws protect players who protect themselves.
